title: Jude and the Spire
premise: Noor Nakamura has survived twenty years in the walled city of Vespergate by being useful and unremarkable: a royal food-taster whose body is a ledger of poisons, and a quiet seller of harmless charms in a city where magic means death. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish on the same night, Noor learns the court beneath the mountain has been buying souls to fuel its wards—and that their late sister's soul was among the first sold. To steal it back, Noor must ally with a disgraced ward-smith, a starless astronomer, and the very prince whose food they taste, risking exposure as an illegal mage. In the end, Noor shatters the mountain court's bargain at the cost of their own hard-won immunity—drinking the one poison that will let them walk into the dark and return with what was stolen—choosing found family and truth over the invisibility that once kept them alive.
about_author: Hazel Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who survive systems designed to erase them.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Noor. A morning of tasting the prince's breakfast establishes Noor's meticulous survival rituals and their secret side trade in charms. When a dish carries a trace of something that shouldn't exist—mountain-iron—they feel the first tremor of change. Emotional beat: wary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Small Magics, Small Prices
chapters.summary: POV Noor. In the night market, Noor sells a luck-knot to a dying lamplighter and refuses payment from a starving child, revealing their code: magic as mercy, never spectacle. A stranger watches too long from the shadows. Emotional beat: tenderness guarded by fear.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The stars extinguish mid-sentence; the border wards fall like cut strings. Panic floods Vespergate. Noor's protective charms burn out all at once, exposing them to any who know how to look. Emotional beat: the vertigo of safety ending.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: POV Sable Ives, disgraced ward-smith turned drunk. Sable recognizes the pattern of the failing wards—not decay but withdrawal, as if something below is pulling power back. He goes looking for the only charm-seller whose work he half remembers. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: An Old Debt in Ash
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Sable confronts Noor; old history surfaces—he testified at the trial that condemned Noor's sister, Wren. Noor denies everything, but that night opens Wren's hidden letter and learns her soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: grief reopened as resolve.

chapters.title: The Prince Who Cannot Sleep
chapters.summary: POV Prince Aurel. Sleepless since the stars went out, Aurel notices his taster flinches at nothing and everything. He tests Noor with a poisoned plum meant for himself and catches the lie in their calm. Emotional beat: isolation recognizing isolation.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Aurel offers a bargain: his protection and access to the royal archive in exchange for Noor's honesty about the falling wards. Noor lies anyway—but takes the deal. Emotional beat: the first compromise of many.

chapters.title: The Archive Below the Waterline
chapters.summary: POV Noor. In flooded archive stacks, Noor finds the original ward charter: the city's protection was purchased, not built, and the payments were souls. Wren's name appears in the oldest ledger. Emotional beat: horror becoming clarity.

chapters.title: Astronomer Without a Sky
chapters.summary: POV Odile Ferrant, court astronomer. With no stars to read, Odile has been charting the darkness itself and found it moving—breathing, almost. She seeks out rumors of a charm-seller. Emotional beat: scientific wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Three Thieves Make a Plan
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor, Sable, and Odile meet in the ruined observatory and map the mountain court's entrance through the old mine shafts. They need a fourth: someone with access to the palace seal. Emotional beat: fragile trust forming around shared theft.

chapters.title: Blackmail Is a Kind of Honesty
chapters.summary: POV Aurel. Noor blackmails the prince with what the archive revealed about his father's reign. Instead of rage, Aurel asks to come along—the mountain took his mother's soul too. Emotional beat: enemies discovering common wounds.

chapters.title: The Last Charm Shop
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Before leaving, Noor burns their stock of charms rather than let the wardens find them, keeping only Wren's luck-knot. The lamplighter's daughter helps cover the traces. Emotional beat: burning the past to fund the future.

chapters.title: Down the Old Veins
chapters.summary: POV Sable. The four descend through abandoned mine shafts where dead wards still twitch like nerves. Sable confesses his testimony against Wren to Noor in the dark; Noor doesn't forgive him, but keeps walking. Emotional beat: unforgiven loyalty.

chapters.title: The City That Eats Light
chapters.summary: POV Odile. They surface inside the mountain court, a cavern city lit by captive soul-fire. Odile realizes the vanished stars are here, caged as lanterns. Emotional beat: awe weaponized into anger.

chapters.title: Servants of the Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Disguised as tribute-bearers, they learn the court's law: every soul sold may be reclaimed by one willing to stake a soul of equal weight. Noor volunteers before thinking. Emotional beat: recklessness born of love.

chapters.title: The Ledger Keeper
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The Ledger Keeper, a figure stitched from contracts, explains the terms: reclaim Wren's soul by dawn of the third day, or forfeit your own. Noor signs. Emotional beat: cold dread under a steady hand.

chapters.title: What Wren Became
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor finds Wren's soul working in the lantern-vaults—dim, fragmented, not the sister they remember. Wren doesn't recognize them. Emotional beat: hope wounded by reality.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Immunity
chapters.summary: POV Noor, flashback woven with present. We learn how Noor became a taster: building poison-immunity deliberately after Wren's execution, preparing, always, for this exact debt. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Prince Plays Courtier
chapters.summary: POV Aurel. While Noor works the vaults, Aurel charms information from the mountain court's ministers and discovers his father renewed the soul-bargain annually. His loyalty to crown collapses. Emotional beat: inheritance as betrayal.

chapters.title: Sable's Second Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Captured by wardens, Sable is offered freedom to testify again—this time against his companions. He stalls, then sabotages the warden-cells instead, freeing other stolen souls as distraction. Emotional beat: redemption chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The Vault of Caged Stars
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile reaches the star-lanterns and begins the slow work of unlocking them, each star she frees weakening the mountain's grip. But the light draws attention. Emotional beat: wonder at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Wren Remembers Rain
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Sitting with fragmented Wren, Noor tells twenty years of stories until one lands—a memory of rain on the shop roof. Wren whispers their childhood name. Emotional beat: grief cracking open into recognition.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The Ledger Keeper declares the bargain breached—someone freed souls early. Wardens sweep the cavern city. The four scatter with hours, not days, left. Emotional beat: panic disciplined into motion.

chapters.title: Through the Minister's Teeth
chapters.summary: POV Aurel. Aurel buys the group time by offering the ministers a false new bargain—his own future reign's tribute. It works, and disgusts him. Emotional beat: self-loathing worn as armor.

chapters.title: The Poison Noor Kept
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor reveals their final preparation: a slow venom, sipped over years, that lets a living body pass through the soul-barrier unharmed—if taken in full dose now. It will burn out their immunity forever. Emotional beat: terror accepted.

chapters.title: Arguments at the Threshold
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The group fights over whether Noor should take the dose; Sable offers his own life instead. Noor refuses them both: 'I spent twenty years getting ready. Let it mean something.' Emotional beat: love expressed as argument.

chapters.title: The Dose
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Alone, Noor drinks the accumulated poison and crosses the barrier into the deep vault where Wren's contract is kept. The world thins to candlelight and ink. Emotional bet: sacrifice embraced without drama.

chapters.title: The Contract Room
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Inside, Noor faces the Ledger Keeper's true form and the original charter bearing their father's signature—the family sold Wren to pay a debt Noor never knew existed. Emotional beat: betrayal upon betrayal.

chapters.title: Tearing the Page
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor cannot steal the contract—it must be voided by consent of the bloodline. Noor consents, signing away their own claim to ever be protected by any ward again. Wren's soul tears free. Emotional beat: truth chosen over safety, theme crystallized.

chapters.title: Collapse of the Mountain Court
chapters.summary: POV multiple, anchored on Odile. With contracts voiding chain-wise, the mountain court unravels; freed stars stream upward through the mine shafts. The four run ahead of the collapse carrying dimming Wren. Emotional beat: exhilaration laced with loss.

chapters.title: The Long Climb Out
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable carries Wren when Noor's poisoned body fails, repaying his testimony with his back and breath. At the last shaft, wardens close in—and Aurel spends his royal seal to hold them. Emotional beat: debts paid in flesh.

chapters.title: Dawn Without Stars
chapters.summary: POV Noor. They surface as the first stars rekindle overhead, released from the mountain. Noor collapses; the poison is winning. Wren, whole but faint, holds their hand and sings the shop-roof song. Emotional beat: arrival at the edge of grief.

chapters.title: What the Taster Cannot Taste
chapters.summary: POV Aurel. Back in Vespergate, Aurel secretly brings Noor to the palace physicians, spending political capital he can't spare. Noor survives, but their immunity is gone—one dish could kill them now. Emotional beat: vulnerability as a new way of living.

chapters.title: Testimony, Third Time
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable testifies publicly—finally truthfully—about the soul-bargain, dismantling the old regime's legitimacy. He expects punishment and receives instead a commission to rebuild the wards honestly. Emotional beat: truth rewarded at last.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Houses
chapters.summary: POV Aurel. Aurel confronts the council with his father's ledgers and dissolves the secret tribute. Some call it treason; the city calls it dawn. He offers Noor a pardon written in their own name, not a false one. Emotional beat: power used as apology.

chapters.title: Wren Learns the New Streets
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Returned after twenty years, Wren navigates a changed city with Noor as guide, both grieving the lost time and greedy for the days left. They reopen the charm shop together—legally, this time. Emotional beat: joy after long hunger.

chapters.title: The First Dish
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor tastes food again for the first time without immunity—flavor as danger and revelation. Aurel eats beside them, sharing the risk as equals. Emotional beat: intimacy built on shared vulnerability.

chapters.title: Charms for a Free City
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Magic is decriminalized; Odile charts a returned sky while the shop fills with customers seeking small wonders. Not everyone forgives mages, and Noor teaches patience to angry neighbors. Emotional beat: healing as slow public work.

chapters.title: The Ledger Burned
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The surviving copy of the soul-ledger is brought to Noor for judgment. They read every name aloud in the market square so the city hears its own debt, then burn it together. Emotional beat: mourning made communal.

chapters.title: Jude and the Spire
chapters.summary: POV Noor, closing frame. On the anniversary, Noor climbs the rebuilt spire with Wren, Sable, Odile, and Aurel, and hangs Wren's luck-knot at the top. Invisible no longer, Noor finally believes survival was only the beginning. Emotional beat: peace earned, family chosen.
